top_three.title: Microsoft says all Microsoft 365 products are operational, ending an outage that disrupted governments, traders, hospitals, and businesses around the world (Bloomberg)
top_three.title_en: Microsoft says all Microsoft 365 products are operational, ending an outage that disrupted governments, traders, hospitals, and businesses around the world (Bloomberg)
top_three.author: Bloomberg
top_three.article_content: Updated on Friday, Nov. 13 at 4:59 a.m. ET / Thursday, Nov. 13 at 1:59 a.m. PT — Microsoft says it's "seeing early stabilization and capacity improvements as recovery actions continue." The company also said it has extended email timeout to 48 hours to help preserve delayed mail during this event.Updated on Friday, Nov. 13 at 1:08 a.m. ET / Thursday, Nov. 12 at 10:08 p.m. PT — Microsoft is still looking into the cause of the outage, but states that at present it is "not aware of any malicious activity that is causing this incident."Updated on Thursday, Nov. 12 at 10:58 p.m. ET / 7:58 p.m. PT — Unfortunately, Microsoft's efforts to bring servers back online aren't going as planned. It appears to have been unable to address the issue of them becoming unresponsive again, and has stated it is now searching for different ways to increase traffic capacity."We've monitored the status of the changes applied to improve serviceability and confirmed they're not taking as expected," Microsoft wrote in an update on X.Updated on Thursday, Nov. 12 at 8:07 p.m. ET / 5:07 p.m. PT — Microsoft has revised its list of features and services impacted by this outage, stating that it is affecting ones that interact with Exchange Online and email services. Microsoft Outlook, SharePoint Online, Teams, Copilot AI, and 365 are all continuing to have various issues, though Azure appears to be operational.Updated on Thursday, Nov. 12 at 7:53 p.m. ET / 4:53 p.m. PT — Microsoft has issued a new update stating that the servers they've brought back online may become unresponsive again when they receive traffic. The company is currently investigating the issue, though in the meantime it's limiting the types of traffic going to these servers in some locations.Updated on Thursday, Nov. 12 at 6:23 p.m. ET / 3:23 p.m. PT —  Microsoft states that it is bringing some servers back online, and "they remain stable so far." Users should expect a "gradual recovery.""We're also shifting traffic to alternate routes wherever possible and observing limited recovery," Microsoft wrote in an update on X. "In parallel, we've streamlined the process of returning the remaining affected servers to service."Updated on Thursday, Nov. 12 at 5:22 p.m. ET / 2:22 p.m. PT — The outage continued into the evening, as Microsoft provided its latest update: "We’re opening all available pathways to restore service, as our actions taken thus far have not provided the anticipated relief."Updated on Thursday, Nov. 12 at 4:21 p.m. ET / 1:21 p.m. PT — On its status page and X account, Microsoft said it has potentially identified some "contributors" to the problem and was deploying fixes. The company said some servers were already back online.Updated on Thursday, Nov. 12 at 3:10 p.m. ET / 12:10 p.m. PT — On its Microsoft 365 Status account on X, the company said it's deploying multiple mitigations to restore service.Updated on Thursday, Nov. 12 at 2:29 p.m. ET / 11:29 p.m. PT — According to the latest updates on the Microsoft service health status webpage, the current issues affect Microsoft 365 business and enterprise customers, not Microsoft's consumer tech products. Updated on Thursday, Nov. 12 at 12:37 p.m. ET / 9:37 p.m. PT— As of this writing, users in multiple regions are still having trouble accessing Microsoft 365. Microsoft customers are reporting problems accessing a variety of the company's software products and services on Thursday afternoon. What services are affected by the ongoing Microsoft outa...
top_three.content_snippet: Microsoft Corp. said access has been fully restored to its flagship software, ending an outage that paralyzed government offices, traders and businesses around the world.
top_three.summary_en: Microsoft experienced a significant global cloud infrastructure failure around November 13, disrupting critical services including Microsoft 365, Outlook, Teams, and SharePoint Online. The company implemented emergency recovery measures such as traffic throttling, route redirection, and extending email timeout thresholds to 48 hours, eventually stabilizing systems while ruling out malicious activity.
top_three.title_zh: 微软全球云服务大面积宕机完成修复
top_three.summary_zh: 微软365全线产品在经历数小时全球性严重服务中断后，目前已恢复运行并实现容量稳步回升

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 微软于北京时间11月13日前后遭遇严重云基础设施故障，导致全球范围内的Microsoft 365、Outlook、Teams及SharePoint Online等关键业务中断。微软采取了包括流量限流、重定向路由以及延长邮件超时限制至48小时等紧急响应措施，目前官方确认系统已恢复稳定并排除恶意攻击因素。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Microsoft experienced a significant global cloud infrastructure failure around November 13, disrupting critical services including Microsoft 365, Outlook, Teams, and SharePoint Online. The company implemented emergency recovery measures such as traffic throttling, route redirection, and extending email timeout thresholds to 48 hours, eventually stabilizing systems while ruling out malicious activity.

elements_zh.what: Microsoft 365及其关联组件遭遇大规模宕机，导致多国政府、医疗及企业系统瘫痪
elements_zh.why: 服务器处理流量能力异常，导致响应失灵，需进行紧急路由切换与容量恢复

elements_en.what: Major outage of Microsoft 365 and related services affecting governments and enterprises worldwide
elements_en.why: Server unresponsiveness under traffic load requiring emergency traffic rerouting and recovery

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此次事件揭示了超大规模云架构在处理瞬时流量拥塞时的脆弱性，单一厂商的过度集约化部署已成为全球数字经济运行的系统性风险点。未来云服务厂商需在容灾架构中引入更细粒度的流量隔离与主动式弹性冗余策略，以降低中心化组件故障引发的级联式崩溃影响。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This incident exposes the inherent fragility of hyper-scale cloud architectures during transient traffic congestion, highlighting the systemic risk posed by over-concentration on a single provider. Future resilience strategies must prioritize granular traffic isolation and proactive elastic redundancy to prevent cascading failures across mission-critical services.

技术应对细节：采取流量限流、调整服务器路由路径，并将邮件接收超时限制延长至48小时
后续影响：排除恶意入侵可能性，正处于逐步恢复容量的稳定运营阶段

Technical response: Traffic throttling, route optimization, and extending email timeout to 48 hours
Status: Malicious activity ruled out; currently in stable recovery and capacity ramp-up

top_three.title: Operand, which offers AI-powered due diligence tools for PE firms, raised $31M across a seed and a Series A led by Khosla Ventures at a $220M valuation (Lucinda Shen/Axios)
top_three.title_en: Operand, which offers AI-powered due diligence tools for PE firms, raised $31M across a seed and a Series A led by Khosla Ventures at a $220M valuation (Lucinda Shen/Axios)
top_three.author: Axios
top_three.article_content:
Operand, which uses AI to do due diligence for private equity firms, raised $31 million in seed and Series A funding, CEO Ram Gorthi tells Axios Pro exclusively.

State of play: It focuses on using non-traditional data sources to help firms get an edge, and AI to process a higher volume of data.
top_three.summary_en: Operand, which uses AI to do due diligence for private equity firms, raised $31 million in seed and Series A funding, CEO Ram Gorthi tells Axios Pro exclusively.

linked_tweets.author: Flames
linked_tweets.content_zh:
告诉人工智能代理它不应该做什么与​​使其在技术上无法做到这一点是不同的。

当人工智能代理处理某人的资金时，这种差异很重要。

您可以告诉代理人避免某些资产、设置支出限额或在出现一定损失后停止交易。但如果它仍然拥有执行交易的广泛权限，那么这些指令就只能到此为止。

通过 MOTES (@meetmotes)，所有者可以设置授权并签署权限。在拟议的交易进行之前，智能账户会根据所有者批准的规则对其进行检查。

因此，代理仍然可以分析市场并制定策略，但它必须在这些限制内运作。它不能只是允许自己在批准的清单之外支出更多资金或交易资产。

我认为这是自主金融更好的基础。赋予代理人做出决策的能力是一回事。确保它仅具有所有者授予的权限也同样重要。
linked_tweets.content_en:
telling an AI agent what it shouldn't do is different from making it technically unable to do it.

when an AI agent is handling someone's money, that difference matters.

you can tell an agent to avoid certain assets, set a spending limit or stop trading after a certain loss. but if it still has broad permission to execute transactions, those instructions only go so far.

with MOTES (@meetmotes), the owner sets the mandate and signs the permissions. before a proposed transaction goes through, the smart account checks it against the rules the owner approved.

so the agent can still analyse the market and come up with strategies, but it has to work within those limits. it can't just give itself permission to spend more or trade assets outside the approved list.

i think this is a better foundation for autonomous finance. giving an agent the ability to make decisions is one thing. making sure it only has the authority the owner gave it is just as important.

linked_tweets.author: Emmanuel
linked_tweets.content_zh:
让人工智能代理获得资本是一回事。准确定义它可以用这笔资金做什么是另一回事。

这是@meetmotes 架构的重要组成部分。

每个 Motes NFT 都连接到一个专用的智能账户，而所有者则定义管理代理行为的权限和限制。

这在资产托管和自动执行之间形成了明确的分离。

代理人不应该对某人的资金拥有无限的权力。它的行动应该保持在所有者设定的范围内。

对我来说，这是自主金融的一个重要设计考虑因素。

情报很重要，但控制执行也同样重要。

一个 NFT，一个 Agent，有自己的账户和明确的边界
linked_tweets.content_en:
giving an AI Agent access to capital is one thing. Defining exactly what it can do with that capital is another.

That's an important part of the @meetmotes architecture.

Every Motes NFT is connected to a dedicated smart account,while the owner defines the permissions and limits that govern the agent's actions.

This creates a clear separation between asset custody and automated execution.

The agent isn't supposed to have unlimited authority over someone's funds. Its actions are meant to stay within the boundaries established by the owner.

For me, this is a crucial design consideration for autonomous finance.

Intelligence matters,but controlled execution matters just as much.

One NFT, one Agent, with its own account and defined boundaries

news.title: Microsoft says all Microsoft 365 products are operational, ending an outage that disrupted governments, traders, hospitals, and businesses around the world (Bloomberg)
news.title_en: Microsoft says all Microsoft 365 products are operational, ending an outage that disrupted governments, traders, hospitals, and businesses around the world (Bloomberg)
news.author: Bloomberg
news.article_content: Updated on Friday, Nov. 13 at 4:59 a.m. ET / Thursday, Nov. 13 at 1:59 a.m. PT — Microsoft says it's "seeing early stabilization and capacity improvements as recovery actions continue." The company also said it has extended email timeout to 48 hours to help preserve delayed mail during this event.Updated on Friday, Nov. 13 at 1:08 a.m. ET / Thursday, Nov. 12 at 10:08 p.m. PT — Microsoft is still looking into the cause of the outage, but states that at present it is "not aware of any malicious activity that is causing this incident."Updated on Thursday, Nov. 12 at 10:58 p.m. ET / 7:58 p.m. PT — Unfortunately, Microsoft's efforts to bring servers back online aren't going as planned. It appears to have been unable to address the issue of them becoming unresponsive again, and has stated it is now searching for different ways to increase traffic capacity."We've monitored the status of the changes applied to improve serviceability and confirmed they're not taking as expected," Microsoft wrote in an update on X.Updated on Thursday, Nov. 12 at 8:07 p.m. ET / 5:07 p.m. PT — Microsoft has revised its list of features and services impacted by this outage, stating that it is affecting ones that interact with Exchange Online and email services. Microsoft Outlook, SharePoint Online, Teams, Copilot AI, and 365 are all continuing to have various issues, though Azure appears to be operational.Updated on Thursday, Nov. 12 at 7:53 p.m. ET / 4:53 p.m. PT — Microsoft has issued a new update stating that the servers they've brought back online may become unresponsive again when they receive traffic. The company is currently investigating the issue, though in the meantime it's limiting the types of traffic going to these servers in some locations.Updated on Thursday, Nov. 12 at 6:23 p.m. ET / 3:23 p.m. PT —  Microsoft states that it is bringing some servers back online, and "they remain stable so far." Users should expect a "gradual recovery.""We're also shifting traffic to alternate routes wherever possible and observing limited recovery," Microsoft wrote in an update on X. "In parallel, we've streamlined the process of returning the remaining affected servers to service."Updated on Thursday, Nov. 12 at 5:22 p.m. ET / 2:22 p.m. PT — The outage continued into the evening, as Microsoft provided its latest update: "We’re opening all available pathways to restore service, as our actions taken thus far have not provided the anticipated relief."Updated on Thursday, Nov. 12 at 4:21 p.m. ET / 1:21 p.m. PT — On its status page and X account, Microsoft said it has potentially identified some "contributors" to the problem and was deploying fixes. The company said some servers were already back online.Updated on Thursday, Nov. 12 at 3:10 p.m. ET / 12:10 p.m. PT — On its Microsoft 365 Status account on X, the company said it's deploying multiple mitigations to restore service.Updated on Thursday, Nov. 12 at 2:29 p.m. ET / 11:29 p.m. PT — According to the latest updates on the Microsoft service health status webpage, the current issues affect Microsoft 365 business and enterprise customers, not Microsoft's consumer tech products. Updated on Thursday, Nov. 12 at 12:37 p.m. ET / 9:37 p.m. PT— As of this writing, users in multiple regions are still having trouble accessing Microsoft 365. Microsoft customers are reporting problems accessing a variety of the company's software products and services on Thursday afternoon. What services are affected by the ongoing Microsoft outa...
news.content_snippet: Microsoft Corp. said access has been fully restored to its flagship software, ending an outage that paralyzed government offices, traders and businesses around the world.
news.summary_en: Microsoft experienced a significant global cloud infrastructure failure around November 13, disrupting critical services including Microsoft 365, Outlook, Teams, and SharePoint Online. The company implemented emergency recovery measures such as traffic throttling, route redirection, and extending email timeout thresholds to 48 hours, eventually stabilizing systems while ruling out malicious activity.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 微软于北京时间11月13日前后遭遇严重云基础设施故障，导致全球范围内的Microsoft 365、Outlook、Teams及SharePoint Online等关键业务中断。微软采取了包括流量限流、重定向路由以及延长邮件超时限制至48小时等紧急响应措施，目前官方确认系统已恢复稳定并排除恶意攻击因素。

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此次事件揭示了超大规模云架构在处理瞬时流量拥塞时的脆弱性，单一厂商的过度集约化部署已成为全球数字经济运行的系统性风险点。未来云服务厂商需在容灾架构中引入更细粒度的流量隔离与主动式弹性冗余策略，以降低中心化组件故障引发的级联式崩溃影响。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This incident exposes the inherent fragility of hyper-scale cloud architectures during transient traffic congestion, highlighting the systemic risk posed by over-concentration on a single provider. Future resilience strategies must prioritize granular traffic isolation and proactive elastic redundancy to prevent cascading failures across mission-critical services.

news.title: Sources: despite Nvidia's 20+ years of business in China, Jensen Huang struggled to gain access to policymakers driving Beijing's chip self-sufficiency campaign (Eleanor Olcott/Financial Times)
news.title_en: Sources: despite Nvidia's 20+ years of business in China, Jensen Huang struggled to gain access to policymakers driving Beijing's chip self-sufficiency campaign (Eleanor Olcott/Financial Times)
news.author: Financial Times
news.article_content:
Jensen Huang's yearslong push to sell chips to China is now colliding with an affair, board investigation, and crisis at Nvidia. At the center is Alice Huang, who has been an executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed, a company that US authorities suspect of helping China access AI chips barred by export controls.

Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing. US officials believe Alice Huang, who has no relation to the Nvidia CEO, was recruited to gather information for Beijing, The New York Times has reported. Nvidia's board is investigating whether Jensen Huang was the target of a "foreign intelligence effort." The episode turns a personal scandal into a test of one of tech's biggest fights: whether the US should prioritize open markets for chip companies or constrain them in the name of national security.

Over the years, Jensen Huang has been bullish on the Chinese market and has said that excluding Nvidia would strengthen Chinese rivals. The board's investigation now places his dealings with Megaspeed, his advocacy for China, and his role in US AI policy under fresh scrutiny. Nvidia says it has no reason to believe company secrets or national security were compromised.

The company's handling of Jensen Huang's future will signal how seriously it takes the risks surrounding America's most important AI chip executive. Here's what Jensen Huang has said about China in recent years.

Amid tightening US semiconductor export controls, this investigation forces a critical re-examination of Nvidia’s China market strategy and the compliance risks of executive interactions with geopolitically sensitive entities.

黄仁勋多年来一直致力于向中国出售芯片，但现在却与英伟达的婚外情、董事会调查和危机发生了冲突。核心人物是爱丽丝·黄（Alice Huang），她曾担任英伟达客户 Megaspeed 的高管，美国当局怀疑这家公司帮助中国获取受出口管制禁止的人工智能芯片。

Megaspeed 否认有不当行为。据《纽约时报》报道，美国官员认为，与英伟达首席执行官没有关系的爱丽丝·黄（Alice Huang）被招募来为北京收集信息。英伟达董事会正在调查黄仁勋是否是“外国情报活动”的目标。这一事件将个人丑闻变成了对科技界最大斗争之一的考验：美国是否应该优先考虑芯片公司的开放市场，还是以国家安全的名义限制它们。

多年来，黄仁勋一直看好中国市场，并表示排除英伟达将增强中国竞争对手的实力。该委员会的调查现在将他与 Megaspeed 的交易、他对中国的倡导以及他在美国人工智能政策中的作用置于新的审查之下。英伟达表示，没有理由相信公司机密或国家安全受到损害。

该公司对黄仁勋未来的处理将表明该公司对这位美国最重要的人工智能芯片高管所面临的风险有多么认真。以下是黄仁勋近年来对中国的评价。

news.title: WhiteMatter, which builds "guardian" AI agents to oversee file access, software use, decision making, and actions of existing AI agents, raised a $20M Series A (Alice Tecotzky/Business Insider)
news.title_en: WhiteMatter, which builds "guardian" AI agents to oversee file access, software use, decision making, and actions of existing AI agents, raised a $20M Series A (Alice Tecotzky/Business Insider)
news.author: Business Insider
news.article_content:
A startup using AI agents to keep rogue AI in line has raised $20 million. WhiteMatter, founded in 2024 and formerly known as QuilrAI, has built agents that oversee what a company's existing AI agents can access, do, and share. The startup spawns one "guardian agent" for each AI agent in an enterprise, which ensures the original agent acts as intended.

Before a company lets an agent access files, use software, make a decision, or trigger an action, WhiteMatter's agent checks whether that's allowed. The so-called guardian also monitors outcomes. Guardian agents scale automatically — when an enterprise creates a new AI agent, a new guardian agent pops up, too.

"Our existing stack wasn't built for agents being the main actor in the story," Vidit Arora, the startup's 35-year-old founder and CEO, told Business Insider. "Organizations are going now from humans being the core actor to agents being the core actor, and our entire tool stack wasn't built for that." Arora said that his company has helped customers transition from human-first to agent-first organizations.

He says we're "not even at the tip of the iceberg" when it comes to agent attacks and compromises, both from external and internal agents. Agentic security has become an increasingly important topic as enterprises grant more non-technical employees access to AI agents capable of completing tasks.

A recent string of agent-powered security incidents has pumped new urgency into the cybersecurity space that WhiteMatter operates in. Other startups have pounced on the business opportunity in agent security, and WhiteMatter's competitors include Onyx Security, Zenity, and Noma. The guardian agents don't run on customers' tokens, but rather on WhiteMatter's self-hosted AI model and GPUs.

The company charges customers a flat rate based on a techy version of AUM: agents under management. Business growth is organic, Arora said, since companies continue to invest in more agents and therefore need more guardian agents. Current customers include Fortune 200 and Fortune 500 companies, such as the asset management firm Alter Domus.

Whitematter, whose new name is a nod to the brain's connective tissue, says it has 2.25 million agents under management to date, and has overseen more than 116 billion AI interactions. Blumberg Capital led WhiteMatter's $20 million Series A funding, and existing investors Crew Capital and Sprout & Oak also participated.

Arora plans to use a big portion of the money to hire for go-to-market and sales roles, and expects his 80-person team to grow by 50% in the next 12 months. He also intends to use the fresh capital to invest in his research team. Read the pitch deck WhiteMatter used to raise its Series A round.

news.article_content_zh:
一家利用人工智能代理来控制流氓人工智能的初创公司已筹集 2000 万美元。 WhiteMatter 成立于 2024 年，以前称为 QuilrAI，它构建了代理来监督公司现有的 AI 代理可以访问、执行和共享的内容。该初创公司为企业中的每个人工智能代理生成一个“监护代理”，以确保原始代理按预期运行。

在公司允许代理访问文件、使用软件、做出决定或触发操作之前，WhiteMatter 的代理会检查是否允许这样做。所谓的监护人也监督结果。监护代理会自动扩展——当企业创建新的人工智能代理时，也会弹出一个新的监护代理。

该初创公司 35 岁的创始人兼首席执行官维迪特·阿罗拉 (Vidit Arora) 告诉 Business Insider：“我们现有的堆栈并不是为充当故事主角的特工而构建的。” “组织现在正在从人类作为核心角色转变为代理作为核心角色，而我们的整个工具堆栈并不是为此而构建的。”阿罗拉表示，他的公司帮助客户从以人为本的组织转变为以代理为先的组织。

他说，当涉及来自外部和内部代理的代理攻击和妥协时，我们“甚至还没有到达冰山一角”。随着企业向更多非技术员工授予能够完成任务的人工智能代理的访问权限，代理安全已成为一个越来越重要的话题。

最近发生的一系列代理安全事件给 WhiteMatter 所在的网络安全领域带来了新的紧迫性。其他初创公司也纷纷抓住代理安全领域的商机，WhiteMatter 的竞争对手包括 Onyx Security、Zenity 和 Noma。监护代理不是在客户的代币上运行，而是在 WhiteMatter 的自托管人工智能模型和 GPU 上运行。

该公司根据技术版本的 AUM（受管理的代理）向客户收取统一费率。阿罗拉表示，业务增长是有机的，因为公司继续投资更多的代理人，因此需要更多的监护代理人。目前的客户包括财富 200 强和财富 500 强公司，例如资产管理公司 Alter Domus。

Whitematter 的新名字是对大脑结缔组织的致敬，该公司表示，迄今为止，它管理着 225 万个代理，并监督了超过 1160 亿次人工智能交互。 Blumberg Capital 领投了 WhiteMatter 的 2000 万美元 A 轮融资，现有投资者 Crew Capital 和 Sprout & Oak 也参与其中。

Arora 计划用大部分资金来招聘市场营销和销售职位，并预计他的 80 人团队将在未来 12 个月内增长 50%。他还打算利用新资金投资他的研究团队。阅读 WhiteMatter 用于筹集 A 轮融资的宣传材料。
fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】WhiteMatter（创始人Vidit Arora）、Blumberg Capital：融资2000万美元用于扩充团队，推广其实时监控AI代理行为的守护架构
【起因与机理】AI代理化进程加速带来前所未有的安全风险，现有的传统安全栈无法应对代理主体驱动的任务流
【关键数据与实测】WhiteMatter融资2000万美元，引入“代理下的管理”（AUM）收费模式。
【各方立场与态度】AI代理安全赛道已进入与Onyx Security、Zenity等厂商的直接竞争阶段。
fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] WhiteMatter (Founder Vidit Arora), Blumberg Capital: Raised $20M Series A to scale its guardian agent architecture for AI oversight
[Root Cause & Mechanism] Rising security incidents with autonomous agents have made traditional security stacks inadequate for agent-driven workflows
[Key Metrics] WhiteMatter raises $20M and introduces an 'Agents Under Management' (AUM) revenue model.
[Key Position & Outlook] Entry into a competitive landscape against players like Onyx Security and Zenity.

news.title: Cambridge, UK-based Tendrils, which is designing a CPU architecture with thousands of cores operating in parallel, raised $30M led by Benchmark (John Reynolds/Tech.eu)
news.title_en: Cambridge, UK-based Tendrils, which is designing a CPU architecture with thousands of cores operating in parallel, raised $30M led by Benchmark (John Reynolds/Tech.eu)
news.author: Tech.eu
news.content_snippet: Tendrils Compute is one of several UK chip startups which investors are backing. — A UK startup developing a radically different type …
news.summary_en: Cambridge-based Tendrils Compute has raised $30 million in a round led by Benchmark. The company is developing a novel high-performance CPU architecture featuring thousands of parallel cores, aiming to deliver superior compute density and energy efficiency for intensive AI workloads compared to traditional general-purpose processors.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 总部位于英国剑桥的Tendrils Compute完成3000万美元融资，由Benchmark领投。该公司致力于研发一种全新的高性能CPU架构，通过数千个内核并行运作的方式，试图在处理高强度AI负载时提供超越传统处理器的算力密度与能效表现。

elements_en.what: Raised $30M to develop a multi-thousand-core parallel CPU architecture for AI workloads
elements_en.why: Seeking architectural breakthroughs to address the performance and throughput bottlenecks of traditional CPUs in AI computing

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 在AI推理负载激增背景下，处理器架构正从“通用优先”转向“吞吐优先”。Tendrils试图通过超大规模并行CPU架构模糊CPU与GPGPU的界限，若其能解决片上互联与内存带宽墙的复杂性，将对当前依赖GPU构建的AI计算基础设施形成有效互补或替代。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Amid surging AI inference demand, processor architecture is pivoting from 'general-purpose priority' to 'throughput priority.' Tendrils aims to blur the lines between CPUs and GPGPUs via massive parallelization. If they can overcome the complexities of on-chip interconnects and memory bandwidth walls, they could offer a potent alternative or complement to the current GPU-centric AI infrastructure.

news.title: JD.com completes its takeover of German electronics retailer Ceconomy, after acquiring a ~60% stake for ~$1.5B, following the EU's approval of the deal (Tomoko Wakasugi/Nikkei Asia)
news.title_en: JD.com completes its takeover of German electronics retailer Ceconomy, after acquiring a ~60% stake for ~$1.5B, following the EU's approval of the deal (Tomoko Wakasugi/Nikkei Asia)
news.author: Nikkei Asia
news.article_content:
SHANGHAI -- JD.com has completed an acquisition of German consumer electronics retailer Ceconomy, aiming to link European physical and online stores using the know-how that the e-commerce company has cultivated in China.

JD.com bought roughly 60% of Ceconomy's shares for 1.34 billion euros ($1.47 billion), according to an announcement Thursday.

Together with the stake retained by JD.com partner Convergenta, an asset management company for Ceconomy's founding family, their combined ownership is now 85%.

After the acquisition was announced last year, the European Commission launched an investigation into whether China's preferential treatment for JD.com, including government subsidies, may hurt fair competition within the European Union. Beijing pushed back against the probe.

On Nov. 3, the European Commission approved the acquisition, with the condition that intra-group transactions be conducted on market terms and that JD.com offer services on the same terms to companies other than Ceconomy.

JD.com's sales of home appliances span online and brick-and-mortar stores. In March, it launched the Joybuy e-commerce site for Europe.

The company is expected to collaborate more closely with Ceconomy, which operates more than 1,000 home appliance stores in Europe including MediaMarkt and Saturn.
news.content_snippet: SHANGHAI -- JD.com has completed an acquisition of German consumer electronics retailer Ceconomy, aiming to link European physical and online stores using the know-how that the e-commerce company has cultivated in China.
news.summary_en: JD.com has completed its acquisition of roughly 60% of German consumer electronics retailer Ceconomy for €1.34 billion ($1.47 billion). Approved by the European Commission under fair market conditions, the deal combines JD's Chinese e-commerce expertise with Ceconomy's network of over 1,000 European stores, including MediaMarkt and Saturn.

news.article_content_zh:
上海讯 —— 京东集团已正式完成对德国消费电子零售巨头 Ceconomy 的收购，旨在利用其在中国本土积累的电商运营与全渠道零售经验，打通欧洲线下实体门店与线上商业生态。

根据周四发布的官方声明，京东以约 13.4 亿欧元（约合 14.7 亿美元）的价格收购了 Ceconomy 约 60% 的股份。

结合京东合作伙伴 Convergenta（Ceconomy 创始家族的资产管理公司）持有的股份，双方在 Ceconomy 的合计持股比例已达 85%。

该项收购于去年首次公布后，欧盟委员会随即展开深入反垄断调查，重点审查中国对京东的产业政策及相关补贴是否会破坏欧盟单一市场的公平竞争环境；北京方面此前对该调查提出了抗辩。

11月3日，欧盟委员会正式批准了该笔收购交易，但附加了严格的市场监管条件，要求京东集团内部交易必须严格遵循市场化公允原则，且京东必须以同等商业条件向 Ceconomy 以外的第三方竞争对手开放相关供应链与技术服务。

京东在家电及消费电子领域的销售网络覆盖线上与线下全渠道。今年3月，京东正式在欧洲上线了 Joybuy 跨境电商平台。

完成交割后，京东将与 Ceconomy 展开全面深度协同。Ceconomy 目前在欧洲全境运营着超过 1000 家大型消费电子实体连锁门店，旗下核心品牌包括知名零售巨头 MediaMarkt 与 Saturn。

【商业与财务细节】欧盟委员会批准交易并设置了关联交易公允市价条件。
【各方立场与态度】京东入主欧洲老牌零售巨头Ceconomy，展现了中国互联网出海由单纯跨境卖货转向深度整合海外本土成熟零售供应链与实体渠道的战略跃升。

news.title: US officials say Trump is not expected to raise allegations of a Chinese intelligence operation involving Jensen Huang during his upcoming meeting with Xi (Dan Mangan/CNBC)
news.title_en: US officials say Trump is not expected to raise allegations of a Chinese intelligence operation involving Jensen Huang during his upcoming meeting with Xi (Dan Mangan/CNBC)
news.author: CNBC
news.article_content:
President Donald Trump is not expected to raise allegations of a Chinese intelligence operation involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang during his upcoming meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, senior U.S. officials said Friday.

Officials also said that Elon Musk, the CEO of Tesla and SpaceX, will accompany Trump on the trip to Shenzhen, China, for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit on Nov. 18 and 19.

The White House, earlier Friday, said Trump plans to have a three-way summit there with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Jensen Huang's relationship with the suspected spy, Alice Huang, who is not related to him, has raised concerns that a Singapore-based company where she was an executive diverted restricted Nvidia chips to China.

"The situation with Nvidia should not really have any bearing on the trip," an official said on the press call, speaking on the condition that they not be identified.

"In all of our discussions and negotiations with the Chinese, we do not negotiate American export controls ... and we don't expect it to figure at all in any of our conversations with the Chinese while we're there."

Asked if Trump would raise the allegations against Alice Huang to Chinese leader Xi Jinping, the official said, "The focus of a meeting with President Xi, at least on the economic side, is going to be about implementation of the trade agreement."

"When it comes to some of these national security matters and examinations and investigations that are going on in the U.S., [that is] probably not something that we're going to read the Chinese in on at this moment," the official said.

Another official said, "I don't expect the president to raise it — the Alice Huang issue."

China has called the allegations against Alice Huang baseless.

Huang resigned this week as Nvidia's CEO after damning reports that he had an affair with Alice Huang, who was an executive of Megaspeed, a cloud-computing company that is being eyed for possible facilitation of sending billions of dollars worth of Nvidia chips in violation of U.S. restrictions on those chips.

The scandal has rocked Nvidia and raised questions about whether the Commerce Department, which is led by Howard Lutnick, has been aggressive enough at blocking advanced chips from ending up in China.

During Friday's call, a reporter asked why Musk was going on the trip with Trump.

"I don't want to speak for the president on exactly why Elon's going," an official said.

"Obviously, he has tremendous business interests in the U.S.-China relationship. He's a big part of our national security," the official said. "There are numerous reasons, given the engagement that the president is going to have, where I think Elon would be of tremendous benefit, just even as an advisor to the president."

美国高级官员周五表示，预计唐纳德·特朗普总统在即将与中国国家主席习近平会面时不会提出涉及英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋的中国情报行动的指控。

官员们还表示，特斯拉和SpaceX首席执行官埃隆·马斯克(Elon Musk)将陪同特朗普前往中国深圳，参加11月18日至19日举行的亚太经合组织峰会。

白宫周五早些时候表示，特朗普计划在那里与习近平和俄罗斯总统普京举行三方峰会。

黄仁勋与涉嫌间谍的爱丽丝黄（与他没有亲属关系）的关系引发了人们的担忧，她曾担任高管的一家新加坡公司将受限制的英伟达芯片转移到中国。

一位官员在新闻发布会上表示，“英伟达的情况应该不会对这次旅行产生任何影响”，但要求不具名。

“在我们与中国人的所有讨论和谈判中，我们不会就美国的出口管制进行谈判……而且我们也不希望它出现在我们在那里与中国人的任何对话中。”

当被问及特朗普是否会向中国领导人习近平提出对黄爱丽的指控时，该官员表示，“与习近平主席会面的重点，至少在经济方面，将是关于贸易协定的实施。”

这位官员表示：“当涉及到美国正在进行的一些国家安全问题以及检查和调查时，我们目前可能不会向中国人了解这些内容。”

另一位官员表示，“我不认为总统会提出爱丽丝黄问题。”

中国称针对黄爱丽的指控毫无根据。

本周，黄仁勋辞去了英伟达首席执行官的职务，此前有报道称，黄仁勋与云计算公司 Megaspeed 的高管爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 有染，该公司正被视为可能违反美国对这些芯片的限制，协助发送价值数十亿美元的英伟达芯片。

这一丑闻震惊了英伟达，并引发了人们对霍华德·卢特尼克领导的商务部在阻止先进芯片进入中国方面是否足够积极的质疑。

在周五的电话会议中，一名记者询问马斯克为什么要与特朗普一起旅行。

一位官员表示：“我不想代表总统解释埃隆离职的具体原因。”

【起因与机理】旨在维护贸易协议推进及避免敏感技术安全调查干扰宏观经济谈判
【调查与监管诉求】特朗普访华行程不会讨论英伟达芯片出口违规调查。
【各方立场与态度】马斯克随行增加科技产业话语权重。

[Root Cause & Mechanism] Prioritizing trade agreement implementation and minimizing interference from sensitive national security probes
[Regulatory & Investigation Focus] Trump to bypass Nvidia chip investigation during China trip.
[Key Position & Outlook] Musk's participation signals tech industry influence in diplomatic missions.

news.title: Tesla says "select customers" can now place orders for its Cybercab "for personal use", for $30K plus a required $299/month Autonomy Subscription to operate (Kara Carlson/Bloomberg)
news.title_en: Tesla says "select customers" can now place orders for its Cybercab "for personal use", for $30K plus a required $299/month Autonomy Subscription to operate (Kara Carlson/Bloomberg)
news.author: Bloomberg
news.article_content:
And it only works inside Tesla’s Robotaxi service areas in Texas and Florida, the same geofences that have turned out to be significantly smaller than what Tesla advertises.

Tesla’s official Robotaxi account announced the invites on X on Friday with screenshots of the order page and the invitation email.

The order page lists the Cybercab at $29,990 before taxes, with an estimated delivery of December 2026 in Austin, Texas. You need to put down a $1,000 non-refundable deposit to order.

The rest is what we already knew. Two seats, a 21-inch center touchscreen, 20.1 cubic feet of cargo space, and no steering wheel or pedals. Tesla calls it “fully autonomous” and says you’ll “manage your ride in the app.”

Musk had promised a Cybercab “below $30,000” when he unveiled it in 2024. He technically hit it. He just didn’t mention the $3,588 a year it takes to use it. Over five years, that’s about $47,600 for a two-seater, before insurance, maintenance, taxes, and charging.

Tesla runs its Robotaxi service in eight cities: Austin, Dallas, Houston, Fort Worth, and San Antonio in Texas, and Miami, Orlando, and Tampa in Florida. That’s where a Cybercab can operate. Everywhere else, it’s a $30,000 sculpture in your driveway.

And those service areas aren’t what Tesla says they are. Independent tracker Koby Pierce tested thousands of addresses in the Robotaxi app and found that the areas where Tesla actually accepts pickups and drop-offs are only 59% to 78% of the advertised geofences in the six cities he checked. In Austin, the very city where Tesla is delivering these cars, it’s about 59%.

Railroad crossings are a big reason why. In Houston, the creator of Robotaxi Tracker found the app quoting about 40 minutes to go two blocks downtown because the vehicle appeared to route around rail crossings. Tesla also lists San Antonio’s airport inside its polygon but doesn’t serve it.

Then there’s the regulatory cloud. NHTSA has ordered Tesla to prove under oath that a car with no brake pedal meets federal safety standards that require one. Tesla answered on October 30 and asked that the entire response be kept confidential. NHTSA hasn’t ruled. Tesla is now selling the car to consumers anyway.

I think this is going to be a total mess. It looks like Tesla is only doing this by invitation and delivering it in Austin to prove they can deliver an “unsupervised” vehicle in 2026.

Tesla is going to sell these to fans who are excited about owning a self-driving car, and many of them will find out the limitations aren’t worth $299 a month on top of a $30,000 car.

Sure, if your monthly Uber bill is well over $300 and you live and work deep inside the geofence, maybe the math works on paper. Until you realize you have to park it somewhere once you get to your destination. Or that it can’t take you to a friend’s place two neighborhoods over. Or that a 15-minute drive turns into an hour because the car won’t cross a train track. With an Uber or a Waymo, that’s someone else’s problem. With a Cybercab, you’re paying for the privilege.

No point trying to calculate what it will cost over X years. Tesla can change that monthly fee at will anyway (and shall be expected to, considering their overall pricing history).

And here’s the part that makes no sense to me. The Cybercab runs on the same AI4 computer as the current Model Y. Tesla already runs unsupervised Model Y Robotaxis in these same geofences. So why can’t the Model Y owners who already paid for “Full Self-Driv...

news.article_content_zh:
而且它只能在特斯拉位于德克萨斯州和佛罗里达州的 Robotaxi 服务区内工作，这些地理围栏实际上比特斯拉宣传的要小得多。

特斯拉官方 Robotaxi 账户周五在 X 上公布了邀请函，并附有订单页面截图和邀请邮件。

订单页面列出的 Cyber​​cab 税前售价为 29,990 美元，预计将于 2026 年 12 月在德克萨斯州奥斯汀交付。您需要支付 1,000 美元的不可退还押金才能订购。

剩下的就是我们已经知道的了。两个座位、21 英寸中央触摸屏、20.1 立方英尺的货物空间，没有方向盘或踏板。特斯拉称其为“完全自主”，并表示您将“在应用程序中管理您的骑行”。

马斯克在 2024 年推出 Cyber​​cab 时曾承诺其售价“低于 30,000 美元”。从技术上讲，他做到了。他只是没有提到使用它每年需要花费 3,588 美元。五年内，一辆两座车的费用约为 47,600 美元（不含保险、维护、税费和收费）。

特斯拉在八个城市提供 Robotaxi 服务：德克萨斯州的奥斯汀、达拉斯、休斯顿、沃斯堡和圣安东尼奥，以及佛罗里达州的迈阿密、奥兰多和坦帕。这就是 Cyber​​cab 可以操作的地方。在其他地方，它就是你车道上的一个价值 30,000 美元的雕塑。

这些服务区域并不像特斯拉所说的那样。独立追踪者 Koby Pierce 在 Robotaxi 应用程序中测试了数千个地址，结果发现，在他检查的 6 个城市中，特斯拉实际接受接送的区域仅为广告地理围栏的 59% 至 78%。在特斯拉交付这些汽车的城市奥斯汀，这一比例约为 59%。

铁路道口是一个重要原因。在休斯顿，Robotaxi Tracker 的创建者发现该应用程序显示，行驶两个街区需要大约 40 分钟，因为该车辆似乎绕着铁路道口行驶。特斯拉还将圣安东尼奥机场列入其多边形内，但不为其提供服务。

然后是监管云。美国国家公路交通安全管理局 (NHTSA) 已命令特斯拉宣誓证明没有制动踏板的汽车符合要求制动踏板的联邦安全标准。特斯拉于 10 月 30 日做出回应，并要求对整个回应保密。 NHTSA 尚未做出裁决。无论如何，特斯拉现在正在向消费者出售汽车。

我认为这将是一团糟。看起来特斯拉只是受邀请才这样做，并在奥斯汀交付，以证明他们可以在 2026 年交付“无人监管”的车辆。

特斯拉将把这些卖给那些对拥有一辆自动驾驶汽车感到兴奋的粉丝，他们中的许多人会发现，除了一辆价值 30,000 美元的汽车之外，这些限制并不值每月 299 美元。

当然，如果你每月的 Uber 账单远远超过 300 美元，并且你在地理围栏深处生活和工作，也许纸上的数学是成立的。直到您意识到到达目的地后必须将其停放在某个地方。或者它不能带你去两个街区外的朋友家。或者因为汽车不会穿过火车轨道，15 分钟的车程变成了一个小时。对于 Uber 或 Waymo，那是别人的问题。使用 Cyber​​cab，您需要为这种特权付费。

尝试计算 X 年内的成本是没有意义的。特斯拉无论如何都可以随意改变月费（考虑到他们的整体定价历史，应该会这样做）。

这是对我来说毫无意义的部分。 Cyber​​cab 与当前的 Model Y 运行在同一台 AI4 计算机上。特斯拉已经在这些相同的地理围栏中运行无人监管的 Model Y Robotaxis。那么，为什么已经支付“全自动驾驶”费用的 Model Y 车主不能在这些区域进行无人监管的操作呢？将其应用到这些已经积累了更多数据的车辆上不是更容易吗？特斯拉不断将这一目标推迟到“明年”，目前大约是 2027 年第二季度，同时要求人们购买一款除此之外别无他用的新双座汽车。

news.title: AI's impact on math is a preview of what AI will do to AI research, with AI matching top human researchers potentially just a couple of years away (Dwarkesh Patel/Dwarkesh Podcast)
news.title_en: AI's impact on math is a preview of what AI will do to AI research, with AI matching top human researchers potentially just a couple of years away (Dwarkesh Patel/Dwarkesh Podcast)
news.author: Dwarkesh Podcast
news.article_content:
00-44:26 Audio playback is not supported on your browser. Please upgrade.Many thanks to Max Farrens, Gabe Fried, and Thomas Larsen for pairing with me through significant parts of writing and researching this essay.

You can watch or listen to me narrate this essay on YouTube, Spotify, and Apple Podcasts.

If you asked me earlier this year how far away we are from superintelligence, I’d probably have said at least the better part of a decade. But over the last three months, I’ve updated my views a ton. I’ve been debating people about this question, both on and off the podcast. And I’ve been watching the progress of AI on verifiable domains and thinking about what that implies for AI research itself.

I’ve now come to the view that we’re only a couple of years away, and possibly only a couple of months away, from AIs that are as good as the best humans at AI research. I’ve also come to believe that automating AI research will compress so much progress into a single year that, soon thereafter (so by 2030, but plausibly as early as next year), we’ll have AIs that are at least as good as the best human experts in every field. I know this is a wild claim, and it’s one that I myself didn’t believe even a couple of months ago. Let me walk you through how my thinking has changed.

Before we get into more speculative arguments, I want to point out that we have a lot of evidence that AI is already dramatically speeding up further AI progress at the frontier.

For example, METR, which is an independent evaluation organization, concluded after three months embedded inside Anthropic that Anthropic’s overall rate of progress on well-scoped tasks is 2x what it was a year ago, and that a “majority of this acceleration today is likely attributable to Anthropic’s extensive use of AI to do R&D.”

OpenAI published a blog post about this in September, where they showed that the heaviest 10% of AI users among OpenAI’s researchers went from using around $1,000 a day of internal coding agents at the beginning of the summer to over $7,000 a day by the end of August.

In September, Anthropic put out a similar post on its own AI uplift. They reported that, as of August, Claude “leads” more than 26% of Anthropic’s AI R&D work—up from under 1% as recently as February.1

Math is a preview of what will happen to AI research When I think about how big a deal it could be if AIs automate AI research, and how soon that could happen, a really important update for me has been just seeing how quickly AI capabilities in mathematics have exploded. Current AIs are slicing through well-scoped problems in mathematics like a hot knife through butter. It was only two years ago that I asked Dario why LLMs aren’t able to use their vast knowledge across so many different fields in order to connect different ideas and make new discoveries. And lo and behold, here we are: In a wholly verifiable domain like mathematics, AIs are doing this search-and-match discovery to such a great extent that hundreds of important results (which the top mathematicians and computer scientists in the world had spent decades trying to resolve) are being churned out as side quests to hype up future model releases.

news.article_content_zh:
00-44:26 您的浏览器不支持音频播放。请升级。非常感谢 Max Farrens、Gabe Fried 和 Thomas Larsen 与我一起完成本文的写作和研究的重要部分。

您可以在 YouTube、Spotify 和 Apple 播客上观看或听我讲述这篇文章。

如果你今年早些时候问我我们离超级智能还有多远，我可能会说至少是十年内的大部分时间。但在过去的三个月里，我更新了很多观点。我一直在播客内外与人们讨论这个问题。我一直在关注人工智能在可验证领域的进展，并思考这对人工智能研究本身意味着什么。

我现在认为，我们距离人工智能研究与人工智能研究中最优秀的人类一样优秀，只需要几年，甚至可能只有几个月的时间。我还开始相信，自动化人工智能研究将在一年内取得如此多的进展，以至于不久之后（到 2030 年，但似乎最早是明年），我们将拥有至少与各个领域最优秀的人类专家一样优秀的人工智能。我知道这是一个疯狂的说法，就连几个月前我自己也不相信。让我向您介绍一下我的想法是如何改变的。

在我们进行更多推测性争论之前，我想指出，我们有大量证据表明人工智能已经极大地加速了人工智能在前沿领域的进一步进步。

例如，独立评估组织 METR 在嵌入 Anthropic 三个月后得出结论，Anthropic 在范围广泛的任务上的总体进度是一年前的 2 倍，并且“今天这种加速的大部分可能归因于 Anthropic 广泛使用人工智能进行研发”。

OpenAI 在 9 月份发表了一篇有关此问题的博客文章，其中显示 OpenAI 研究人员中最重的 10% 的 AI 用户从夏初每天使用内部编码代理的费用约为 1,000 美元，到 8 月底每天使用的内部编码代理的费用超过 7,000 美元。

九月份，Anthropic 就其自己的人工智能提升发表了类似的帖子。他们报告称，截至 8 月，Claude“领导”了 Anthropic 超过 26% 的人工智能研发工作，而 2 月份这一比例还不到 1%。1

数学是人工智能研究将会发生的事情的预览当我想到如果人工智能自动化人工智能研究将会有多大的影响，以及这会发生多久，对我来说一个真正重要的更新就是看到人工智能在数学中的能力爆炸的速度有多快。当前的人工智能正在解决范围广泛的数学问题，就像热刀切黄油一样。就在两年前，我问达里奥，为什么法学硕士无法利用他们在如此多不同领域的丰富知识来连接不同的想法并做出新的发现。你瞧，我们在这里：在数学这样一个完全可验证的领域，人工智能正在很大程度上进行这种搜索和匹配发现，以至于数百个重要结果（世界上顶尖的数学家和计算机科学家花了几十年的时间试图解决这些问题）正在被大量生产出来，作为炒作未来模型发布的支线任务。

我们从 2023 年的“这个模型无法可靠地添加四位数字”到 2024 年的“这个模型几乎无法解决高中数学竞赛中的任何问题”，到 2025 年的“哦，它可以在国际数学奥林匹克竞赛中赢得金牌”，再到今年早些时候的“哇，它正在解决开放式 Erdős 问题，但也许只是因为没有人尝试过”，速度之快真是太疯狂了。来解决这些特定问题，类似的解决方案已经出现在文献中，”大约一个月前，“好吧，它他妈的在 88 小时内解决了千禧年奖问题。”

小说《伊甸园之东》中有一句话：“关于诸神的陨落，有一点是肯定的：他们不会堕落一点；他们会崩溃、粉碎。”

确实，进步不成比例地偏向于数学中充满验证的部分，比如寻找反例（而不是提出新理论）。托比·奥德 (Toby Ord) 最近发表了一篇关于此的精彩文章。他写道，“虽然当前的人工智能系统开始自动化数学证明，但目前几乎没有证据表明它们可以提出强有力的问题或找到深刻的数学探究新领域。”

但同样的观点的另一种说法是：当前的人工智能系统已经解决了千年奖问题，但都没有能力提出强有力的问题或找到深刻的数学探究新领域。

从广义上讲，这种解决范围广泛的问题的能力对于机器学习研究来说比数学更重要。这是因为数学研究的目标不仅仅是证明或反驳一长串猜想，而是扩展人类对数学概念的理解。提出拓扑、群论或笛卡尔网格的概念远比确切地知道可以从 n 个点组成多少个单位对更重要。我们主要关心这些深奥的问题，因为它们可能会引发新的数学理论。

news.title: Doc: Amazon, wary of AI agents favoring sites with better data, plans to gather data on nearly every product sold anywhere, including by crawling rivals' sites (Greg Bensinger/Reuters)

news.author: Reuters
news.content_snippet: Amazon (AMZN.O) has a secret plan to ensure shoppers never need to leave its site: own the world's product information.
news.summary_en: Amazon is developing the 'World Product Graph' project, which plans to crawl competitor websites to index virtually every product sold online. The strategy aims to feed massive data into the Alexa AI shopping assistant, improving response accuracy and ensuring that consumers remain within the Amazon ecosystem even during research phases.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 亚马逊正研发“全球产品图谱”（World Product Graph）项目，计划通过爬取竞争对手电商网站，索引几乎所有在线销售产品。该策略旨在为Alexa AI购物助手提供海量数据，以提升回应准确度，并确保购物者即便在对比搜索时也能被导回亚马逊平台。

news.title: Sources: the FAA outage occurred after an update to the private communications network that connects the ATC system caused the system to reboot and crash (Kierra Frazier/CBS News)
news.title_en: Sources: the FAA outage occurred after an update to the private communications network that connects the ATC system caused the system to reboot and crash (Kierra Frazier/CBS News)
news.author: CBS News

A rare nationwide ground stop on all departing U.S. flights that lasted several hours Friday has been lifted, and flights are resuming, the Federal Aviation Administration said. Officials said the issue stemmed from a "telecommunication outage."

"At 8:15 tonight, Eastern time, we've opened up the airspace," Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said during a news briefing Friday night. "Now does that mean every flight is going to fly right now? It's going to be slow. So if you're watching, you're at an airport, check with your airline."

In a social media post following the briefing, the FAA said that "before clearing flights to resume, we thoroughly tested our systems to confirm they were stable and that operations remain reliable."

The FAA had issued the ground stop on all departing flights due to "extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety." The ground stop lasted about five hours.

Duffy attributed the ground stop to outdated air traffic control technology and routers overloaded by data.

"What we have is an incredibly old air traffic control system," Duffy said during the news conference. " ... Our routers actually got overloaded with data and … they started to give us inconsistency in the data from those routers. And because of that, we shut the system down."

"The FAA lifted the ground stop and some flight departures are resuming," the FAA confirmed in a social media post following the briefing. "Before clearing flights to resume, we thoroughly tested our systems to confirm they were stable and that operations remain reliable."

An update to the private communications network that connects America's air traffic control system caused the system to reboot, leading to a crash and a communications outage, multiple sources told CBS News earlier Friday. The system is operated by L3Harris, which did not immediately respond to CBS News' request for comment.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said in Friday's briefing that new security patches introduced into the older system appeared to "overwhelm" its routers.

Duffy said the FAA would try to move as many flights as possible Friday night depending on crew capacity.

"If not, we're going to start tomorrow [Saturday] morning with our airline partners moving those aircraft. But it's going to take us some time to unwind what's happened this afternoon," Duffy said.

There were more than 10,000 delays and over 4,000 cancellations listed Friday, according to the flight tracking website FlightAware.

Duffy said he thinks flights will be "back up and operational as we come into the heat of travel" during the Thanksgiving holiday later this month.

Mullin told reporters in an earlier briefing outside the White House Friday that "there was no indication, as of yet, that this was a nefarious act against us. It was just a telecommunication outage, as of right now."

"There is no indication, we had no reason to believe, that as of right now, that this was a threat to the United States," Mullin said. "This was a telecommunication outage throughout FAA. Out of an abundance of caution, we have grounded all the flights. And all the flights are accounted for."

Mullin reiterated Friday night that there was no cyberattack and the ground stop was not related to the massive global Microsoft outage.

news.article_content_zh:
美国联邦航空管理局表示，周五持续数小时的所有美国出发航班在全国范围内罕见的地面停留已经取消，航班正在恢复。官员们表示，问题源于“电信中断”。

“东部时间今晚 8 点 15 分，我们开放了领空，”交通部长肖恩·达菲 (Sean Duffy) 在周五晚上的新闻发布会上表示。 “这是否意味着现在每个航班都会起飞？速度会很慢。所以，如果你在机场观看，请咨询你的航空公司。”

美国联邦航空局在简报后的社交媒体帖子中表示，“在批准航班恢复之前，我们彻底测试了我们的系统，以确认它们稳定且运行仍然可靠。”

由于“特殊情况和安全原因”，美国联邦航空局已对所有离港航班发出地面停止令。地面停留持续了大约五个小时。

达菲将这次地面停靠归咎于过时的空中交通管制技术和数据超载的路由器。

达菲在新闻发布会上说：“我们拥有的是非常古老的空中交通管制系统。” “......我们的路由器实际上数据过载......他们开始给我们带来来自这些路由器的数据不一致。因此，我们关闭了系统。”

“美国联邦航空局取消了地面停止，一些航班起飞正在恢复，”美国联邦航空局在简报后在社交媒体上发帖证实。 “在批准航班恢复之前，我们彻底测试了我们的系统，以确认它们稳定且运营仍然可靠。”

周五早些时候，多名消息人士告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，连接美国空中交通管制系统的私人通信网络的更新导致系统重新启动，导致坠机和通信中断。该系统由 L3Harris 运营，该公司没有立即回应哥伦比亚广播公司新闻的置评请求。

国土安全部部长马克韦恩·穆林在周五的新闻发布会上表示，旧系统中引入的新安全补丁似乎“压垮”了其路由器。

达菲表示，美国联邦航空局将根据机组人员容量，在周五晚上尝试调动尽可能多的航班。

“如果没有，我们将于明天（周六）早上开始与我们的航空公司合作伙伴一起转移这些飞机。但我们需要一些时间来解决今天下午发生的事情，”达菲说。

根据航班跟踪网站 FlightAware 的数据，周五有超过 10,000 起延误和超过 4,000 起取消航班。

达菲表示，他认为本月晚些时候的感恩节假期期间，航班将“随着我们进入旅行热潮而恢复并投入运营”。

穆林周五在白宫外举行的早些时候的新闻发布会上告诉记者，“到目前为止，没有迹象表明这是针对我们的邪恶行为。到目前为止，这只是一次电信中断。”

news.title: Amazon has a plan to index the world’s online shopping data
news.title_en: Amazon has a plan to index the world’s online shopping data
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Listing the details of everything for sale everywhere is meant to make Amazon more useful than Reddit for people and AI agents.﻿

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Amazon has plans to build a vault of data on every product sold anywhere on the internet, even products Amazon doesn’t sell, and make the information available through its own site, according to Reuters. The project, called the “World Product Graph,” is meant to make it less likely that shoppers leave Amazon to do their product research on Reddit or Google, and make it more likely shoppers end up at Amazon even if they’re searching for a product sold elsewhere. The same goes for AI agents — if Amazon has the largest stockpile of shopping data, AI agents may rely on its index of products over others, so even people shopping with bots will end up on its pages.

Links to outside retailers’ products have already started popping up on Amazon through the “shop direct” feature it launched last year. The company also has its own AI shopping assistant, Alexa for Shopping, previously called Rufus. The World Product Graph project would also be aimed at fixing issues with the AI by providing it more data. According to Reuters, an internal Amazon document on the project says “Many Rufus answers are factually wrong or incomplete” and running users’ Amazon searches with the AI is expensive. Adding more data is reportedly supposed to make the system more accurate and able to use cheaper models.

Whether this actually ships is still up in the air. The internal document reportedly says the project “depends on discovering how brands organize their products on their own websites,” which could involve Amazon crawling other retailers’ sites. Reuters says it’s unclear “if or when this plan may be implemented,” but said the document on it included an October 1st, 2027 release date.

Amazon said in a statement to Reuters that “Draft, outdated documents often paint an incomplete picture and the existence of a brainstorming document such as this one doesn’t necessarily reflect our current plans.”

该主题的帖子将添加到您的每日电子邮件摘要和主页源中。

列出各地待售商品的详细信息，旨在让亚马逊比 Reddit 对人们和人工智能代理更有用。

该作者的帖子将添加到您的每日电子邮件摘要和主页源中。

亚马逊计划为互联网上任何地方销售的每种产品（甚至亚马逊不销售的产品）建立一个数据库，并通过自己的网站提供这些信息。该项目名为“世界产品图谱”，旨在降低购物者离开亚马逊而在 Reddit 或 Google 上进行产品研究的可能性，并让购物者更有可能最终选择亚马逊，即使他们正在搜索其他地方销售的产品。人工智能代理也是如此——如果亚马逊拥有最大的购物数据库存，人工智能代理可能会比其他人更依赖其产品索引，因此即使是使用机器人购物的人最终也会访问其页面。

通过去年推出的“直接购买”功能，外部零售商产品的链接已经开始在亚马逊上出现。该公司还拥有自己的人工智能购物助手 Alexa for Shopping，以前称为 Rufus。世界产品图项目还旨在通过向人工智能提供更多数据来解决人工智能的问题。据路透社报道，亚马逊关于该项目的一份内部文件称，“许多 Rufus 的答案实际上是错误的或不完整的”，并且使用人工智能运行用户的亚马逊搜索成本高昂。据报道，添加更多数据应该会使系统更加准确并能够使用更便宜的模型。

这是否真的可以发货仍然悬而未决。据报道，内部文件称该项目“取决于发现品牌如何在自己的网站上组织产品”，这可能涉及亚马逊抓取其他零售商的网站。路透社表示，目前尚不清楚“该计划是否或何时实施”，但表示文件中包含了 2027 年 10 月 1 日的发布日期。

亚马逊在给路透社的一份声明中表示，“过时的草稿文件常常描绘出不完整的画面，像这样的集思广益文件的存在并不一定反映我们当前的计划。”

news.title: ChatGPT Wallet lets OpenAI’s Dots agents make purchases for you
news.title_en: ChatGPT Wallet lets OpenAI’s Dots agents make purchases for you
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
After adding a card to the wallet, your Dots agents can use it to buy things in response to your prompts, but they’ll check in with you each time before checking out. OpenAI’s support page says every purchase with ChatGPT Wallet requires a security check with biometric verification like Face ID or a fingerprint scan.

[Image: Users have to approve every purchase from ChatGPT Wallet. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/openai-chatgpt-wallet-approval-pop-up.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]

[Media: https://twitter.com/ChatGPT/status/2121283151729496235?a=Dzv0TkF6sRIc6NCqEso&s=20]

After you review the AI agent’s purchase and sign off on it, OpenAI says that, similar to using tap to pay, Apple Pay, or Google Wallet, it substitutes your credit card details with a payment token, so your actual card info isn’t shared with your Dots agent or the business you’re buying from. Eventually, OpenAI says it expects “users to be able to delegate purchases entirely to their agent by setting clear parameters—such as spending limits, purchase categories, or time periods—and pre-approve those purchases.”

ChatGPT Wallet might not work everywhere. Some retailers have restrictions on AI agents or block them altogether. Earlier this year, Amazon blocked Meta’s Muse agents. OpenAI says that in order for agents to use ChatGPT Wallet, “websites need to ensure agents are not inadvertently blocked, and payment and risk systems need to recognize legitimate purchases made by agents.”

news.article_content_zh:
将卡添加到钱包后，您的 Dots 代理可以根据您的提示使用它来购买东西，但他们每次结帐前都会与您联系。 OpenAI 的支持页面称，每次使用 ChatGPT 钱包进行的购买都需要进行安全检查，包括面部 ID 或指纹扫描等生物识别验证。

OpenAI 表示，在您审核 AI 代理的购买并签字后，与使用触碰支付、Apple Pay 或 Google Wallet 类似，它会用支付令牌替换您的信用卡详细信息，因此您的实际银行卡信息不会与您的 Dots 代理或您要购买的企业共享。最终，OpenAI 表示，它希望“用户能够通过设置明确的参数（例如支出限额、购买类别或时间段）将购买完全委托给他们的代理，并预先批准这些购买。”

ChatGPT 钱包可能无法在所有地方使用。一些零售商对人工智能代理进行了限制或完全阻止。今年早些时候，亚马逊屏蔽了 Meta 的 Muse 代理。 OpenAI 表示，为了让代理商使用 ChatGPT 钱包，“网站需要确保代理商不会无意中被屏蔽，支付和风险系统需要识别代理商的合法购买行为。”

news.title: Jensen Huang's ouster likely traces back to Nvidia's risky business practices more than his personal life
news.title_en: Jensen Huang's ouster likely traces back to Nvidia's risky business practices more than his personal life
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
A WSJ report suggests Jensen Huang was pushed out more over his business practices than over his affairs.

Nvidia built a risky credit program under Huang, the Wall Street Journal reports. The company offered AI cloud providers and data center developers billions of dollars in financial guarantees so they could afford Nvidia chips. Huang's son-in-law Nico Caprez pushed the program and promised partners quick closings. In return, the cloud providers were supposed to give Nvidia a cut of their revenue.

The largest deal involved talks with OpenAI over a $250 billion guarantee for a data center in Ohio. Nvidia shares fell 5% after the deal became public. Interim CEO Colette Kress, who had been CFO, then cut Nvidia's commitment to OpenAI in half. The scaled-back deal was signed in August.Ad

According to the WSJ, Kress had already questioned internally how the guarantees were valued and what they would return and had tried to rein in Caprez. In an August meeting, Huang reportedly called her "a deer in the headlights" and dismissed her as a mere "reporting CFO" who didn't help him with strategy or decision-making. Circular AI deals by Nvidia and other cloud and chip companies have drawn criticism since at least last year for inflating a bubble.Ad

Nvidia's stock valuation also reportedly frustrated Huang. The company's average monthly stock multiple fell from 23 to 16 between May and October, and Nvidia responded with the largest share buyback in its history.

Major cloud providers were planning to adopt alternative chips and reduce their dependence on Nvidia. With Nvidia committed to buying large volumes of wafers and memory, Huang described the threat as an “avalanche” rolling toward the chipmaker.Ad

At the GTC conference in Berlin in October, Huang used a story about a soup vendor in Japan to put pressure on half a dozen cloud CEOs. He said he had stood in a long line and eaten one of the best soups of his life. When he asked for seconds, the vendor said no because too many people were waiting and he was running out of soup. "He's a better businessperson than all of you," Huang told the CEOs, according to the WSJ.

The reasoning behind the story was that the soup vendor didn't sell his whole inventory to one or two customers. He kept prices high and his customer base broad. Huang said the cloud providers weren't following that example and were selling too much compute to a handful of big customers instead of spreading it across many buyers. "You are not establishing the value of my products," Huang said.Ad

Whether Huang left voluntarily because the situation was slipping away from him, which seems unlikely, or whether the board saw an opportunity to use the affairs as leverage, hasn't been reported.Ad

Separately, the spy allegations involving Alice Huang rest on shaky ground, according to CNN. The intelligence gathered so far doesn't prove she actually worked as a spy for Beijing. Even within the US government, there's disagreement about the strength of the evidence.

news.article_content_zh:
《华尔街日报》的一篇报道表明，黄仁勋被驱逐的更多原因是他的商业行为，而不是他的事务。

据《华尔街日报》报道，英伟达在黄仁勋的领导下建立了一项高风险信贷计划。该公司为人工智能云提供商和数据中心开发商提供了数十亿美元的财务担保，以便他们能够买得起 Nvidia 芯片。黄的女婿尼科·卡普雷斯 (Nico Caprez) 推动了该计划，并向合作伙伴承诺快速关闭。作为回报，云提供商应该向英伟达提供一定的收入分成。

最大的一笔交易涉及与 OpenAI 就俄亥俄州数据中心 2500 亿美元的担保进行谈判。交易公开后，英伟达股价下跌 5%。随后，曾担任首席财务官的临时首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯 (Colette Kress) 将 Nvidia 对 OpenAI 的承诺削减了一半。缩减规模的协议于八月签署。

据《华尔街日报》报道，克雷斯已经在内部质疑这些担保的价值以及它们将返回什么，并试图控制卡普雷兹。据报道，在 8 月份的一次会议上，黄称她为“车灯下的鹿”，并斥责她只是一个“汇报的首席财务官”，无法帮助他制定战略或决策。至少从去年开始，英伟达和其他云和芯片公司的循环人工智能交易就因吹大泡沫而受到批评。

据报道，英伟达的股票估值也让黄仁勋感到沮丧。 5 月至 10 月期间，该公司的平均月度股票市盈率从 23 倍下降至 16 倍，英伟达采取了其历史上最大规模的股票回购作为回应。

主要云提供商计划采用替代芯片并减少对 Nvidia 的依赖。随着英伟达承诺购买大量晶圆和内存，黄仁勋将这一威胁描述为向芯片制造商滚滚而来的“雪崩”。

10 月份在柏林举行的 GTC 会议上，黄用一个关于日本汤供应商的故事向六位云首席执行官施加压力。他说他排了很长的队，吃了一生中最好的汤之一。当他要求再来一份时，摊贩拒绝了，因为太多人在等待，而他的汤已经用完了。据《华尔街日报》报道，黄告诉首席执行官们：“他是一个比你们所有人都更好的商人。”

这个故事背后的原因是，汤贩并没有把他的全部库存卖给一两个顾客。他保持高价格并扩大客户群。黄说，云提供商没有效仿这个例子，而是向少数大客户出售过多的计算，而不是将其分散给许多买家。黄说：“你没有确立我产品的价值。”

黄是否自愿离开是因为形势正在从他身边溜走（这似乎不太可能），或者董事会是否看到了利用这一事件作为杠杆的机会，目前尚未报道。

另外，据美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 报道，涉及爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 的间谍指控站不住脚。到目前为止收集到的情报并不能证明她实际上是北京的间谍。即使在美国政府内部，对于证据的强度也存在分歧。

news.title: Microsoft 365 Crawls Back to Life After a 24-Hour Outage
news.title_en: Microsoft 365 Crawls Back to Life After a 24-Hour Outage
news.author: Wired AI
news.article_content:
Sorry, Margaret, your email is working again.

After a widespread outage shut down Microsoft 365 services for businesses, governments, and tens of millions of other users around the world, the essential cloud services are now (mostly) back online, according to the company’s status page.

The outage debacle began around lunchtime on the East Coast on Thursday, with users reporting Outlook outages to the service-tracking website Downdetector just after 12 pm ET. Within the hour, Microsoft said it was investigating reports of an outage that at the time was limited to North America. It quickly spread to impact more than 70 countries around the world.

The full cause of Microsoft’s unprecedented outage remains unknown, but the company repeatedly ruled out a cyberattack as the cause in statements to its status page. It is also ruling out AI or AI agents playing a role in the debacle.

“We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services,” a Microsoft spokesperson says in a statement. “This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents. The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions.”

The company has promised a “full post-incident report” after it has fully reviewed what went wrong.

As Outlook, Teams, Copilot, and other Microsoft 365 systems come back online, users will likely see their inboxes turn into a mess. “You're probably going to get a lot of notifications when things come back,” says Jonathan Leitschuh, an independent researcher.

Microsoft said it had increased the queue time for emails to 48 hours in an attempt to ensure that every message that people tried to send while its systems were down gets delivered. Leitschuh points out that, even with the bulk of systems restored, users may receive “a flood of notifications a few hours down the pike” as subsystems come back online.

The total impact of the Microsoft outage may never be fully known, but it’s safe to say it’s already significant. Governments from Japan to the United States reported disruptions to a bevy of functions. Airlines reported problems with their ability to communicate with customers. Many law enforcement and emergency services ground to a halt. And hospitals reported widespread interruptions to their operations.

Ultimately, the episode serves as a reminder of the risks involved when the whole world relies on a single company for a critical service. “We're very interdependent on these systems in modern life,” says Leitschuh. Next time, delayed emails may be the least of our worries.

根据该公司的状态页面，在大范围的故障关闭了为企业、政府和全球数千万其他用户提供的 Microsoft 365 服务后，基本的云服务现在（大部分）重新上线。

故障灾难始于周四东海岸的午餐时间左右，美国东部时间中午 12 点刚过，用户就向服务跟踪网站 DownDetector 报告了 Outlook 故障。一个小时内，微软表示正在调查当时仅限于北美地区的宕机报告。它迅速蔓延影响全球70多个国家。

微软史无前例的宕机的完整原因尚不清楚，但该公司在其状态页面的声明中一再排除网络攻击的原因。它还排除了人工智能或人工智能代理在这场灾难中发挥作用的可能性。

微软发言人在一份声明中表示：“我们的服务得到了广泛的恢复和稳定。” “这是一个与网络或人工智能/代理无关的技术问题。该事件是由近期网络变更后出现的早期网络容量升级过程中的一个问题引起的。我们已经解决了根本问题，并继续为其余客户和地区恢复服务。”

该公司承诺在全面审查问题原因后提供“完整的事件后报告”。

随着 Outlook、Teams、Copilot 和其他 Microsoft 365 系统重新上线，用户可能会看到他们的收件箱变得一团糟。 “当事情恢复时，你可能会收到很多通知，”独立研究员 Jonathan Leitschuh 说。

微软表示，它已将电子邮件的排队时间延长至 48 小时，以确保人们在系统停机时尝试发送的每条消息都能送达。 Leitschuh 指出，即使大部分系统已恢复，当子系统恢复在线时，用户也可能会“在几个小时内收到大量通知”。

微软宕机的总体影响可能永远无法完全知晓，但可以肯定地说影响已经很严重了。从日本到美国，各国政府均报告称一系列职能受到干扰。航空公司报告称其与客户沟通的能力存在问题。许多执法和紧急服务陷入停滞。医院报告称其运营大范围中断。

最终，这一事件提醒人们，当全世界都依赖一家公司提供关键服务时所涉及的风险。 “在现代生活中，我们非常依赖这些系统，”Leitschuh 说。下次，延迟的电子邮件可能是我们最不用担心的了。

大故事：酷孩子都用小写字母书写——这会让你生气吗？

news.title: OpenAI rebuilt AI shopping from scratch with ChatGPT Wallet
news.title_en: OpenAI rebuilt AI shopping from scratch with ChatGPT Wallet
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
OpenAI is taking a second shot at AI shopping with ChatGPT Wallet, catching up with rivals like Anthropic, Meta, and xAI, whose agents can already shop online.

To get started, users add their card once. Before every purchase, the system displays the items, the total, and the selected card. Users then approve each payment with a security check such as Face ID or a fingerprint.Ad

Neither the agent nor the online store ever sees the real card details. Instead, payment partners American Express, Mastercard, and Visa generate a payment token, a stand-in card number with its own security code. According to OpenAI, existing card rewards and the usual bank protections for eligible disputes still apply. OpenAI plans to eventually let users hand purchases off to their agents entirely, within set spending limits, product categories, and timeframes.Ad

According to OpenAI, a purchase starts with the customer describing what they want, after which ChatGPT searches the open web, APIs, or merchant product feeds for options, and the user compares them and picks one. ChatGPT then completes the purchase either by using a browser on the merchant's existing website or through a plugin that supports structured actions such as managing the cart.

Many websites and payment systems still block AI agents as bots or reject their purchases for security reasons. To address that, OpenAI is also releasing a Commerce Partner Playbook. The guide explains how merchants can adjust their firewalls, provide product data, and work with payment providers such as Stripe, Adyen, and Riskified so agent-driven purchases go through.Ad

OpenAI is playing catch-up on payment features for AI agents. Competitors such as Anthropic's Claude Duet, Meta's Muse, and xAI's Grok Bot already have built-in payments and rely in part on single-use cards via Stripe Link. Google and Perplexity also let users buy through their own checkout tools, such as Google Pay and Instant Buy.

OpenAI 正在利用 ChatGPT 钱包在人工智能购物领域进行第二次尝试，追赶 Anthropic、Meta 和 xAI 等竞争对手，这些公司的代理商已经可以在线购物。

首先，用户只需添加一次卡即可。每次购买前，系统都会显示商品、总计和所选卡。然后，用户通过安全检查（例如面容 ID 或指纹）批准每笔付款。

代理商和在线商店都看不到真实的卡详细信息。相反，支付合作伙伴美国运通卡、万事达卡和维萨卡会生成支付令牌，即带有自己的安全代码的替代卡号。根据 OpenAI 的说法，现有的卡奖励和针对合格争议的通常银行保护措施仍然适用。 OpenAI 计划最终让用户在设定的支出限额、产品类别和时间范围内将购买完全交给他们的代理商。

许多网站和支付系统仍然将人工智能代理视为机器人，或出于安全原因拒绝其购买。为了解决这个问题，OpenAI 还发布了商业合作伙伴手册。该指南解释了商家如何调整防火墙、提供产品数据以及与 Stripe、Adyen 和 Riskified 等支付提供商合作，以便完成代理驱动的购买。

news.title: Banks bar Chinese and Hong Kong investors from Anthropic IPO over US export controls
news.title_en: Banks bar Chinese and Hong Kong investors from Anthropic IPO over US export controls
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Investors from mainland China and Hong Kong are being shut out of Anthropic's IPO, according to Bloomberg. Multiple banks have reportedly rejected buy orders from those regions or consider allocations unlikely, with some of the people involved citing ITAR, the US export control rules governing defense-related goods, as the reason. Anthropic declined to comment.

Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are leading the offering, with 20 other banks involved. The stock is expected to trade on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT after pricing on November 18.

The company's products aren't officially available in China or Hong Kong, and its broader relationship with the country has been defined by confrontation. Anthropic has blocked firms under Chinese control from its AI services and is fighting workarounds that let Chinese companies access Claude Code. It also exposed large-scale distillation attacks by DeepSeek, Moonshot, and MiniMax involving some 16 million queries.AdAd

news.title: Anthropic's Claude for Manufacturing plugs AI directly into factory software to automate industrial workflows
news.title_en: Anthropic's Claude for Manufacturing plugs AI directly into factory software to automate industrial workflows
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Anthropic has released Claude for Manufacturing, a plugin giving the AI direct access to industrial software to automate factory workflows. The new solution connects via four universal interfaces to Autodesk Fusion, Oracle NetSuite, Microsoft 365, and Infor. Other systems can be integrated through file exports to Microsoft 365.

With 17 specific skills, the AI drafts quotes from actual inventory, compares suppliers, generates quality reports and design variants, and analyzes sensor data and manuals during machine downtime. Via an added Infor plugin, Claude can also order from backup suppliers when deliveries are delayed and reschedule production—after human approval. All results are linked to original source documents for employee review before reaching customers or suppliers.

The plugin is available to Team and Enterprise customers but doesn't control physical machines yet. For that, Anthropic is separately developing the Model Hardware Standard as a research preview, connecting AI agents to devices like robotic arms and microscopes via standardized drivers. This cuts setup time from weeks or months to hours or minutes but still requires human oversight due to the AI's limited grasp of physical processes.AdAd

news.title: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights
news.title_en: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights
news.author: Ars Technica
news.article_content:
“SignDrop” exploit lets local users gain all-powerful System rights.

Nightmare Eclipse, the pseudonym of a researcher with an ongoing, very public beef with Microsoft, has dropped yet another Windows zero-day.

On Tuesday, Nightmare Eclipse disclosed SignDrop, a vulnerability that gives local users full System rights on some versions of Windows. The vulnerability resides in the Common Log File System, which Microsoft describes as a “general-purpose logging service used by software clients running in user-mode or kernel-mode.” By forcing a privileged process such as Windows Defender to open a crafted CLFS container, an attacker with ordinary user rights can abuse the privileged file creation to elevate privileges to System.

The attack exploits the interaction of CLFS, Windows Defender, and Windows file permissions. The exploit uses Windows Defender to open a log file created by a standard user by calling ServerMpUpdateEngineSignature, a legitimate Defender function for processing antivirus signature updates.

By manipulating Windows Object Manager symbolic links, the attacker causes Defender to open the CLFS container in the security context of the antimalware engine. If an associated authentication file is missing, CLFS creates it using Defender’s System privileges. Because CLFS assigns the newly created file the Discretionary Access Control List of the original file, the attacker may gain access to a file created with System privileges, allowing the file-creation operation to be abused as part of a privilege-escalation attack.

Ironically, the vulnerability stems from a security measure Microsoft introduced in October 2025 to prevent attackers from exploiting other vulnerabilities in CLFS.

“If everything is chained correctly, funnily this legit security mitigation can be used against itself and allow an elevation [of] privileges,” Nightmare Eclipse wrote. “Everything is done properly by Microsoft here but the logic allows abuse.”

What makes it funnier is the fact that it can be used against any antimalware engine to bypass their self defense (or tamper protection) mechanism as you can trigger arbitrary file creation in the context of their own antimalware process so from the perspective of their kernel drivers, the file creation request is coming from their own legit process so it passes, this makes this vulnerability unique as it can be used to turn off any antivirus/EDR.

Nightmare Eclipse said the exploit worked against Windows 11 26H2, Windows 11 26H2 Experimental, and Windows Server 2025 Experimental. People can see if their systems are vulnerable by checking the CLFS authentication mode. If it’s in learning mode or enforcement mode, the system is vulnerable, and the PoC supplied in the post should spawn a SYSTEM shell. Nightmare Eclipse has published numerous other Windows zero-days in recent months.

Researcher Will Dormann said in an interview that he has been able to reproduce the exploit and that it works as described, but not on all versions of Windows 11. But there’s a catch, he said.

“The requirements are important in that it seems to require Windows 26H2, and one that has existed for more than 90 days, it seems,” he explained. “That is, you can’t just take a new 26H2 system and install updates and have it work.”

key_points_en: Key Development: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights

news.article_content_zh:
“SignDrop”漏洞让本地用户获得全能的系统权限。

Nightmare Eclipse 是一名研究人员的化名，该研究人员一直在公开地与微软发生争执，该公司又发布了另一个 Windows 零日漏洞。

周二，Nightmare Eclipse 披露了 SignDrop，这是一个为本地用户提供某些 Windows 版本的完全系统权限的漏洞。该漏洞存在于通用日志文件系统中，微软将其描述为“在用户模式或内核模式下运行的软件客户端使用的通用日志服务”。通过强制 Windows Defender 等特权进程打开精心设计的 CLFS 容器，具有普通用户权限的攻击者可以滥用特权文件创建来将权限提升到 System.

该攻击利用 CLFS、Windows Defender 和 Windows 文件权限的交互。该漏洞利用 Windows Defender 打开标准用户通过调用 ServerMpUpdateEngineSignature 创建的日志文件，ServerMpUpdateEngineSignature 是用于处理防病毒签名更新的合法 Defender 函数。

通过操纵 Windows 对象管理器符号链接，攻击者使 Defender 在反恶意软件引擎的安全上下文中打开 CLFS 容器。如果关联的身份验证文件丢失，CLFS 将使用 Defender 的系统权限创建它。由于 CLFS 为新创建的文件分配原始文件的自主访问控制列表，因此攻击者可能会获得对使用系统权限创建的文件的访问权限，从而允许文件创建操作被滥用作为权限升级攻击的一部分。

讽刺的是，该漏洞源于微软于 2025 年 10 月推出的一项安全措施，旨在防止攻击者利用 CLFS 中的其他漏洞。

Nightmare Eclipse 写道：“如果一切都正确链接，有趣的是，这种合法的安全缓解措施可以用来对付自身，并允许特权提升。” “微软在这里所做的一切都是正确的，但逻辑允许滥用。”

更有趣的是，它可以用于对抗任何反恶意软件引擎，以绕过其自我防御（或篡改保护）机制，因为您可以在其自己的反恶意软件进程的上下文中触发任意文件创建，因此从其内核驱动程序的角度来看，文件创建请求来自其自己的合法进程，因此它会通过，这使得该漏洞独一无二，因为它可用于关闭任何防病毒/EDR。

Nightmare Eclipse 表示，该漏洞适用于 Windows 11 26H2、Windows 11 26H2 Experimental 和 Windows Server 2025 Experimental。人们可以通过检查 CLFS 身份验证模式来了解自己的系统是否存在漏洞。如果处于学习模式或强制模式，系统很容易受到攻击，并且帖子中提供的 PoC 应该会生成一个 SYSTEM shell。近几个月来，Nightmare Eclipse 发布了许多其他 Windows 零日漏洞。

研究员 Will Dormann 在接受采访时表示，他已经能够重现该漏洞，并且其工作原理与描述的一样，但并非在所有版本的 Windows 11 上都有效。但他说，有一个问题。

“这些要求很重要，因为它似乎需要 Windows 26H2，而且这个版本似乎已经存在了 90 多天，”他解释道。 “也就是说，你不能只采用新的 26H2 系统并安装更新并让它工作。”

Dormann 表示，要使系统容易受到攻击，HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\CLFS\Authentication\Mode 值必须为 0 或 1。在多曼使用的众多机器中，只有一台满足这一要求。

微软确实分阶段推出了 Windows 更新，例如 26H2，因此尚不清楚有多少人拥有它。您可以通过运行“winver”命令进行检查。在这篇文章发布后发布的一份声明中，微软表示正在调查该文章，并且没有证据表明该漏洞正在被利用。该公司还表示，Defender 会阻止潜在的利用尝试。

这个故事已更新以添加微软的评论。

news.title: Jensen Huang and the End of the Founder Fairy Tale
news.title_en: Jensen Huang and the End of the Founder Fairy Tale
news.author: Wired AI
news.article_content:
It was July of 2024, and Jensen Huang was punchy.

I had agreed to travel to Denver, Colorado, to interview the Nvidia CEO at SIGGRAPH, the annual confab of computer graphics PhDs and practitioners. Early that year I’d conducted a lengthy sit-down interview with Huang for a WIRED magazine feature, which apparently went well enough—both for WIRED and for Nvidia’s executive communications team—that I had been asked to interview Huang again at this conference. Another opportunity to grill the CEO of the modern world’s most consequential company? Yes, of course. I began preparing.

What ensued was, in a word, bizarre. During the first prep call for the conference, the type of call-in which PR handlers typically try to coax specific questions out of journalists to prevent an ambush, a youngish, vaguely familiar woman took the lead. This was Madison Huang, Jensen’s daughter. She was clearly intelligent, commanding respect. She told me about the slides Jensen would be presenting on stage at SIGGRAPH and offered suggestions for key moments when I might tee him up to talk about the slides.

Slides? Tee up Jensen? What kind of “interview” was this?

I raised my concerns with both my editors and Nvidia. We agreed that I would ask the questions I intended to ask him, which included questions about the environmental impact of data centers, and that Huang would also be referring to slides. Let’s just say the interview didn’t go smoothly. (It’s on YouTube.) To this day, former and current Nvidia workers sometimes tell me that I “handled” the whole thing well. Huang was domineering, evaded some of my questions, and, immediately after our session concluded, did an impromptu Q&A session with a much more adoring crowd than me. Then I was guided offstage, and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg hopped on, where he and Huang had a lovey-dovey fireside chat.

As a longtime journalist I’m used to occasional adversarial interactions; I really don’t lose sleep over them. This was just a CEO being a CEO. Huang later agreed to meet with me again, in December 2024. But that interview in Denver had underscored for me how much Jensen Huang wanted to control the narrative. Not just wanted to; he assumed he would. And to a large extent he did. Until this week.

Narrative has always been a critical part of Huang’s success. He was not just your average electrical engineering nerd who toiled away on something that would eventually find a product-market fit. By Huang’s own telling, he was an immigrant founder, an underdog, a wife guy who chased (and eventually married) his college sweetheart, a scrappy startup guy who dined at Denny’s in the early days. A visionary who worked Sundays and who didn’t sleep well because he always heard the hoof steps of competitors. A parent who brought his kids into the corporate fold. A man who loved Nvidia so much he tattooed an abstract version of the company logo on his arm.

Huang built the highest-valued publicly traded company in history. That part’s not just fairy tale. It’s true. Now, it’s starting to read more like a Greek tragedy.

Back in January 2024, when I sat down with him for our first-ever in-person meeting, Huang right off the bat talked about the importance of storytelling. Here’s an excerpt:

Jensen Huang: Somebody who I really admire, as a leader and a person, is Shantanu Narayen, the CEO of Adobe. He said he always wanted to be a journalist because he loved telling stories.

news.article_content_zh:
那是 2024 年 7 月，黄仁勋精力充沛。

我同意前往科罗拉多州丹佛市，在 SIGGRAPH（计算机图形学博士和从业者的年度会议）上采访 Nvidia 首席执行官。那年早些时候，我为《连线》杂志的一篇专题文章对黄进行了一次长时间的静坐采访，显然这次采访对《连线》和 Nvidia 的高管沟通团队来说都进展顺利，以至于我被邀请在这次会议上再次采访黄。另一个拷问现代世界最有影响力的公司首席执行官的机会吗？是的当然。我开始准备。

总之，接下来发生的事情很奇怪。在会议的第一次准备电话会议中，公关人员通常试图向记者提出具体问题以防止伏击，在这种电话会议中，一位年轻的、有点熟悉的女性带头。这是詹森的女儿麦迪逊·黄。她显然很聪明，值得尊敬。她告诉我 Jensen 将在 SIGGRAPH 舞台上展示的幻灯片，并为我可能邀请他谈论幻灯片的关键时刻提供建议。

幻灯片？詹森打球吗？这是一次什么样的“采访”？

我向我的编辑和 Nvidia 提出了我的担忧。我们同意我会问我想问他的问题，其中包括有关数据中心对环境影响的问题，黄也会提到幻灯片。只能说面试进行得并不顺利。 （在 YouTube 上。）直到今天，前任和现任 Nvidia 员工有时都会告诉我，我“处理”了整个事情。黄很霸道，回避了我的一些问题，并且在我们的会议结束后立即与比我更崇拜的人群进行了即兴问答。然后我被引导下台，Meta 首席执行官马克·扎克伯格跳上车，他和黄在炉边进行了一场恩爱的谈话。

作为一名资深记者，我习惯了偶尔的敌对互动；我真的不会因为他们而失眠。这就是首席执行官的本质。黄后来同意在 2024 年 12 月再次与我会面。但在丹佛的那次采访向我强调了黄仁勋多么想控制叙事。不只是想要；他以为他会的。在很大程度上他做到了。直到本周。

叙事一直是黄的成功的关键部分。他不仅仅是普通的电气工程书呆子，他们为最终找到适合产品市场的东西而辛勤工作。根据黄自己的说法，他是一位移民创始人，一个失败者，一个追逐（并最终结婚）大学恋人的妻子，一个早期在丹尼餐厅用餐的斗志旺盛的创业者。一个周日工作的有远见的人，因为总是听到竞争对手的马蹄声而睡不好觉。一位将孩子带入公司的父母。一个非常热爱英伟达的人，他在手臂上纹了公司徽标的抽象版本。

黄建立了历史上价值最高的上市公司。这部分不仅仅是童话故事。这是真的。现在，它开始读起来更像是希腊悲剧。

早在 2024 年 1 月，当我与他第一次面对面会面时，黄立即谈到了讲故事的重要性。这是摘录：

黄仁勋：作为领导者和个人，我真正敬佩的人是 Adob​​e 的首席执行官 Shantanu Narayen。他说他一直想成为一名记者，因为他喜欢讲故事。

连线：能够有效地讲述自己的故事似乎是建立企业的重要组成部分。

是的。战略制定就是讲故事。文化建设就是讲故事。

你曾多次说过，你并没有根据宣传材料推销 Nvidia 的想法。

这是正确的。这实际上是为了讲故事。

news.title: Nearly 70 percent of US agencies use generative AI, and unions are finally catching up with guardrails
news.title_en: Nearly 70 percent of US agencies use generative AI, and unions are finally catching up with guardrails
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
US public-sector unions are winning more protections against AI surveillance and automation-driven job losses. The issue is growing more urgent as nearly 70 percent of US government agencies already use generative AI, according to an Ernst and Young survey.

The wins are piling up nationwide. After a strike vote in October, IFPTE Local 21 in Oakland secured retraining programs instead of AI-related layoffs. In Pennsylvania, Governor Josh Shapiro guaranteed SEIU Local 668 human oversight during a pilot of OpenAI's ChatGPT Enterprise. The Transport Workers Union in Ohio won veto power over autonomous vehicles. On top of that, California Governor Gavin Newsom banned AI surveillance software, often called "bossware," along with automated firings in September. New York has protected state employees from AI displacement by law since late 2025.

Employers are pushing automation to cut costs, according to labor researcher Kung Feng at UC Berkeley. Union leaders like Liz Shuler of the AFL-CIO, Lorena Gonzalez, and TWU's John Samuelsen support AI safety systems where they help workers but insist on mandatory human control over every AI application in the workplace, the Guardian reports.AdAd
